narrative.overview:
You put a part down on the bench to check it. The light is neutral, the edges are true and the callouts are exact. Everything J3D draws serves that moment:

- The chrome is a quiet frame of cool near-black.
- The viewport is a soft graphite gradient that lets any part colour read.
- One blue, Selection Blue, marks only what the user is acting on: the selected part, the tool that's on, the measured   edge.

The mood is **quiet, exact and workmanlike**. Precision shows in the numbers and in the drawing, not in decoration. The numbers use tabular figures, always carry their unit, and give lengths to three decimals. The drawing puts near-black BREP edges over every face.

Controls say what they do. Tools carry a label beside their icon wherever the window has room, and everything is written in sentence case. Controls are square-cornered and stay grey until they're used. A tool that's on takes a blue tint; a setting, such as the selection mode or the projection, is shown by a quietly raised segment, never in blue. The density is a desktop tool's: a 48 px bar, a 320 px model list and 13 px detail text. It never gets crowded, though: there's one row of tools in labelled groups, one floating panel and one view cube.

J3D is dark only (PRODUCT.md). The chrome is built from MudBlazor 9 components, restyled in `J3DTheme.cs` and `app.css`. Material's UPPERCASE labels, round icon buttons and filled-blue toggles were replaced on purpose (2026-10-25), so new work doesn't bring them back.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only, with cool near-black neutrals: hue about 258°, OKLCH chroma under 0.02.
One accent, Selection Blue, for what's being acted on. Settings and chrome are grey.
Flat chrome separated by 1 px hairlines. Shadows only on what floats.
The system font stack, in sentence case. Numbers in tabular figures, with their units.
The model is the brightest thing on screen.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Selection Blue marks what the user is acting on (the selection, the hover, a tool that's on, the measurement, progress, focus) and nothing else. A mode or setting that's merely chosen is never blue. There's no decorative blue and no second accent.

rules.name: The Model Is Brightest Rule
rules.body: The chrome stays within the graphite neutrals, so the model is the brightest thing on screen, in its own colours or in Part Grey. Bars, panels and snackbars are never filled with colour.

rules.name: The Status Means Status Rule
rules.body: Amber and coral appear only for warnings, failures and the destructive confirmation, and in snackbars only on the icon. Never use them for emphasis or decoration.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, button, heading and menu item is written in sentence case, as the README is. Capitals are for names and formats (STEP, BREP, GLB) and keys (H, Shift+H), not for emphasis.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number the user reads as a value is set in tabular figures: measurements, move fields and the labels in 3D. Its unit is written after it (mm, °, mm²). Lengths have three decimals, angles two, and mesh values are prefixed ≈. In the panel, values are right-aligned, and whole parts of five or more digits are grouped in thousands with a narrow space ("12 500.000 mm³"). A copied value keeps its plain form.

rules.name: The Weight Ceiling Rule
rules.body: 500 is the heaviest weight in the chrome. The only exception is the view cube's labels, which are drawn on the canvas at 600. Emphasis comes from Text Bright against Text Muted, not from bold.

rules.name: The One Bar Rule
rules.body: Every global tool lives in the app bar's single row, in its group, and the row stays on one line from 900 px up. A new tool joins a group. It doesn't get a second row or a floating toolbar.

rules.name: The Fixed Corners Rule
rules.body: Each viewport corner has one owner: the view and its settings top right, the panel bottom left, and snackbars bottom right. Nothing else goes in those corners.

rules.name: The Say It Rule
rules.body: A tool that's a verb of the product (Measure, Move, Origin frames, the selection modes) shows its name whenever the window has room. An icon alone is for actions whose icon everyone already reads (hide, show, undo, redo), and every icon has a tooltip naming the action and its key.

rules.name: The Shadows Only When Floating Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this sits above the page and will go away": a menu, a dialog, a snackbar. Bars, rows and panels stay flat, with hairlines.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Reference Rule
rules.body: A dashed Selection Blue outline means "the reference" (a measurement's first pick) or "drop here". A solid outline is the current result.

dos: Do use Selection Blue (#4F9DFF) only for the selection, the hover, a tool that's on, measurement graphics, progress and focus.
Do write every label in sentence case, and give each product verb (Measure, Move, Origin frames, Model, Object, Feature) its name beside its icon wherever there's room.
Do keep the chrome in the graphite neutrals, and separate regions and toolbar groups with 1 px Hairline (#2A2F36) borders.
Do give every icon-only button an accessible name and a tooltip naming the action and its key, and write the key beside menu commands too.
Do show values in tabular figures with their unit: lengths to 3 decimals, angles to 2, ≈ before mesh values, and long whole numbers grouped in thousands for reading.
Do float new viewport UI on 92% Surface Slate with a hairline and a 6 px radius, in the corner that owns it.
Do open confirmations with Cancel focused, and say when Undo can bring something back.
donts: Don't add a light theme, a theme toggle, or light surfaces. PRODUCT.md makes dark only binding.
Don't bring back UPPERCASE labels, round icon buttons or filled-blue toggles.
Don't show a chosen setting or mode in blue; raise it quietly instead.
Don't load fonts, icons or images from another origin. Cross-origin isolation blocks them, so use the system stack and bundled or inline assets.
Don't add a second accent colour, gradients in the chrome, or coloured fills on bars, panels or snackbars.
Don't mark a selected or active row with a coloured bar at its edge; tint it.
Don't put shadows on bars, the drawer, rows or the floating panel. Shadows are for menus, dialogs and snackbars.
Don't use Warning Amber or Error Coral for anything but warnings, failures and the destructive confirmation.
Don't use Text Faint (#5C636E, 2.9:1) for text the user needs to read.
Don't add a second toolbar row. The app bar stays on one line from 900 px up.
